metadata.title: Claude, Funding Digest.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: does Claude already know what belongs in a good funding digest, or does something have to tell it? Lands the carry-out that a skill gives Claude one exact recipe, not editorial judgment, and outside that recipe Claude has nothing written down to follow.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed Claude already knows what belongs in a good funding digest. Not quite — it has to be told, in a file it reads before acting. Here's what that file actually spells out.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types the naive framing, hesitates on 'KNOWS', corrects to 'has to be told', lands the real question

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md. Writer types the newcomer's wrong-guess word 'KNOWS' (implying Claude already possesses editorial judgment about what belongs in a digest), hesitates, corrects to 'has to be told' -> lands 'Claude already has to be told what a good funding digest should say, right?'. The wrong guess is picked up directly by B01's 'file it reads before acting' framing. Narration is 34 words + lead_silence_s 0.8, giving the typing a >=9s window (TIMING LAW).

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is funding-digest. The SKILL.md contains the full instruction set — plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.

props.title: A skill is a folder.
props.calloutText: The SKILL.md is the instruction set.

beats.narration_text: The pipeline is in the Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and executes it. Linear — no branching unless the step says so.

Ask for exactly what the file names — a funding digest for the sectors or companies you're watching — and you get the same one-page slide, with the same fields, every time. Ask for something the file never mentions — a different format, a metric it doesn't list — and there's nothing else backing it up. The file is the entire spec.

shot.new_visual_element: Two columns: what the file names, what it never mentions — no verdict frame, per-item facts only

props.sparkLine: Named triggers get the same slide. Anything else has no spec to follow.
leftItems: deal flow digest, weekly recap, capital markets update — the exact trigger phrases
links back to the source deals in Capital IQ
rightItems: what happens if there's no new activity in your watched sector that week
no other output format is named — no doc, no multi-slide deck
no freshness window for "recent" is defined
any request outside those trigger phrases has nothing to fall back on

beats.narration_text: A skill doesn't make Claude judge what's newsworthy. It gives Claude one exact recipe — and outside that recipe, Claude has nothing written down to follow.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Pick a report or slide you regularly ask for — a weekly recap, a status digest, anything you repeat. Before you ask Claude to write it, list every field and trigger phrase you actually expect it to cover. Then ask Claude to produce it, and check whether anything you expected is missing, or whether it added something you never asked for.
